key_insight: Anchoring MLLM adaptation to entity-grounded visual evidence preserves the model's temporal localization ability under visual domain shift, enabling robust cross-domain Video Temporal Grounding without full fine-tuning.
problem_solved: Fine-tuning multimodal LLMs for video temporal grounding often fails under visual domain shift—EVIDENT prevents the decoupling of temporal localization and entity attention, reducing cross-domain performance degradation and heavy retraining.
method: Extract entity-grounded visual evidence (object/person regions, tracks, or localized features) aligned with the textual query from video frames.
Route lightweight, parameter-efficient adapters into the frozen MLLM so the model conditions temporal localization on the selected visual evidence while preserving learned localization behavior.
Train a routing mechanism to select and fuse entity evidence with temporal prediction heads, improving generalization to unseen visual domains with minimal parameter updates.
impact: Practitioners get a parameter-efficient way to make MLLMs for VTG robust across visual domains—reducing retraining cost and improving reliability of video-grounding systems in real-world, cross-domain deployments.
visual_elements: Model diagram: frozen MLLM backbone + adapter/routing modules showing evidence flow from detected entities into temporal grounding head.
Before/after bar chart: in-domain vs cross-domain VTG accuracy comparing standard fine-tuning vs EVIDENT.
Frame timeline: attention heatmap across frames highlighting entity regions used to predict the target temporal segment.
Routing schematic: decision flow showing how entity evidence is selected and injected into the adapter pathways.
paper_title: EVIDENT: Routing MLLM Adaptation through Entity-Grounded Visual Evidence for Cross-Domain Video Temporal Grounding
paper_authors: Geo Ahn, Jiwook Han, Youngrae Kim, Joonseok Lee, Jinwoo Choi
